title: How water is made clean
examples: Teacher, what is the first thing that happens to dirty river water?
Can you explain the difference between filtering and disinfecting water?
Why do we need a whole water treatment plant?

explain.say: Today we learn how dirty water becomes clean water.
Next, the water goes through settling tanks to let heavy things drop.
Then, the water passes through filters to catch smaller bits of dirt.
Finally, we disinfect the water to kill any tiny germs that remain.
A whole water treatment works combines all these steps in order.
When you see a tap running clear water you know this process worked well.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of screening?
faq.a: Screening removes the very large pieces of rubbish from the raw water. It stops big items from damaging the equipment later on.
asks: Does screening remove all the junk?
What is the first step for dirty water?

faq.q: Why do we need the settling stage?
faq.a: Settling lets heavier dirt and grit fall to the bottom of a tank by gravity. This makes the water clearer before filtering.
asks: How do we get the heavy stuff out?

faq.q: Is filtering enough to make water safe to drink?
faq.a: No, filtering only removes dirt particles, not invisible germs. Disinfecting is needed to kill those tiny living things.

faq.q: What is disinfection, and why is it important?
faq.a: Disinfection usually uses chemicals like chlorine to kill harmful bacteria and viruses. This makes the water safe for people to drink.
asks: How do they kill the germs?

faq.q: Are these steps always done in this exact order?
faq.a: Yes, generally, the process must follow this order to be effective. You must remove big stuff before you remove small stuff.

facts: Screening removes large debris like sticks and leaves.
Settling uses gravity to let heavy solids sink to the bottom.
Filtering uses layers of sand and gravel to catch smaller particles.
Disinfection kills harmful microorganisms like bacteria.

quiz.say: If the water has large sticks and rags in it, which step must happen first?
quiz.why: Screening is designed specifically to catch large floating items before anything else.

wrong.0: Settling only works on things that are heavy enough to sink, not big sticks.
wrong.1: Filters are designed for small particles, not large floating rubbish.
wrong.2: Disinfecting only kills germs, it does not remove physical objects.

quiz.say: After the water has settled and the dirt has dropped, what is the next physical cleaning step?
quiz.why: Filtering uses materials like sand to trap the smaller suspended dirt particles left after settling.

wrong.0: Disinfecting is a chemical step to kill germs, not a physical cleaning step.
wrong.1: Storage is where the clean water waits, it is not a cleaning step itself.
wrong.3: Screening happens at the very beginning to remove the largest items.

quiz.say: If the water looks clear but you are worried about invisible germs, what final step must you perform?
quiz.why: Disinfecting uses chemicals to kill invisible germs that the physical steps missed.

wrong.0: Settling only removes visible, heavy dirt particles.
wrong.1: Filtering is good for dirt, but not necessarily for all germs.
wrong.2: Screening only removes large objects like sticks and leaves.
